title: Zonal traffic fabric with cost-aware preemptive shedding and SLO isolation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our current region failover and geo‑pinning logic reacts to outages and latency after customer requests have already experienced degradation. That leads to SLO burn for high‑priority tenants and uneven cost exposure when we spill to more expensive capacity. Goal: implement a zonal traffic fabric that combines latency‑based routing, soft geo‑pinning, and capacity/cost signals to preemptively shed or steer traffic before SLOs are violated.

Scope and objectives:
- Define per‑zone SLO isolation windows (example: regional P99 target 450ms for gen-text endpoint; tenant SLOs derived as P99 <= 1.2x regional baseline).
- Build a lightweight fabric that tracks real‑time capacity tokens per zone (in-flight requests, spool queue depth, GPU utilization) and a cost signal reflecting on‑demand vs reserved vs burst pricing.
- Implement two steering primitives: (1) latency‑preferring hedging: replicate small requests to local + nearest neighbor when latency tail is predicted to exceed threshold, (2) cost‑aware preemptive shedding: when capacity tokens drop below soft threshold and predicted SLO burn > threshold, shed low‑priority or best‑effort traffic gracefully.
- Integrate circuit breaker gates with graded backoff and automated local evictions to avoid catastrophic cross‑region spill.

Design highlights and unique ideas:
- Zonal token buckets: each AZ/zone maintains a sliding capacity token count (derived from running average of free GPU queue slots and recent successful concurrency). Tokens propagate to global fabric as soft hints — not authoritative — to support degraded control‑plane scenarios.
- Cost tags on steer decisions: requests carry a "cost-priority" label (e.g., reserved, burst, spot, free‑trial). The fabric uses this to prefer routing to cheaper zones and to pick which requests to preemptively shed under pressure.
- Predictive SLO guardrails: short horizon (30s) skyline predictor uses rate of change in P95/P99 and queue growth to estimate SLO burn probability. When P(burn) > 0.6 we enter preemptive mode.
- Circuit breaker tiers: soft CB (metrics window 30s, threshold 2x baseline error rate OR latency tail multiplier 1.5) triggers hedging and rate‑limit reduction; hard CB (5min aggregated breach OR sustained queue growth) triggers local ejection and capacity reservations for priority traffic.

Trade-offs considered:
- Replication/hedging increases cost and can worsen congestion if used indiscriminately. Mitigation: only hedge sub‑64 token requests and cap hedged fraction per tenant to 2% by default.
- Token propagation adds control plane load. Mitigation: use compressed signals (hot zone deltas) and fallback to conservative defaults when control plane is slow.
- Cost tags require instrumentation across API/Console/SDK. We'll start with server‑side inference and a fallback mapping for legacy requests.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Primary SLOs: regional P99 for small gen requests <= 450ms (95% of regions over 30d) and tenant SLO retention rate >= 99% across planned failovers.
- Safety metrics: cross‑region spill ratio for priority customers <= 0.5% under steady state; hedging cost delta <= +3% for production baseline.
- Operational metrics: time to detect capacity depletion < 20s; circuit breaker activation false positive rate < 1 in 10k.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Instrumentation & simulator (2 sprints): implement zonal tokens, cost tags, and a traffic simulator to model hedging/shedding outcomes. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/zonal-fabric-spec (draft).
2) Control plane API + local fabric (1 sprint): endpoint to query token hints and publish local CB state (protobuf + REST).
3) Canary runtime changes (1 sprint): implement hedging and cost‑aware shed hooks behind feature flag. Canary in 2 non‑critical regions with non‑enterprise tenants.
4) Full rollout + policy tuning (2 sprints): expand and refine thresholds; integrate with Console dashboards and alerting.

Testing and rollout safeguards:
- Start with synthetic traffic and chaos (zone CPU/GPU spike) in our staging cluster, validate that preemptive shedding reduces SLO burn vs control.
- Gradual tenant rollouts: phase customers by priority class, ensure rollback path can immediately re‑enable original regional pinning.
- Observability: new console panel "Zonal Fabric" with per‑zone tokens, hedging rate, shed events, and per‑tenant cost delta.

Open questions / signoffs needed:
- Assignment of tenant cost‑priority mapping (PM decision needed for default handling of free trials and partner tiers).
- Exact numerical thresholds for token levels and P(burn) — will be tuned from simulator.
- Whether to expose an opt‑out for customers that mandate regional residency (legal/regulatory).

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/zonal-fabric-spec
- Simulator notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/simulators/zonal-fabric-sim.ipynb
- Proposed PR templates and starter branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/PR-4238

Longer term ideas (future epics):
- Integrate spot/commit price forecasts to proactively shift bulk best‑effort workloads to cheaper regions during troughs.
- Expose a per‑tenant SLA contract API so customers can opt into aggressive cost reductions in exchange for lower availability commitments.

2026-03-13 - Marco Nguyen: Canary feature flag toggled in region eu‑west‑2 for 2% low‑priority traffic. Early telemetry shows 18% reduction in regional P99 for hedged tenants and +0.9% cost delta. Continuing to monitor.
